EXAM:
CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Persistent cough. History of smoking. Pulmonary nodule
identified on prior examination.

COMPARISON:
CT chest dated 11/10/2025.

TECHNIQUE:
Contrast-enhanced CT images of the chest were obtained from
the thoracic inlet through the upper abdomen.

FINDINGS:
LUNGS AND AIRWAYS:
8 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the posterior right upper
lobe, previously measuring 6 mm. Mild bibasilar dependent
atelectatic change. No focal airspace consolidation.

PLEURA:
No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

MEDIASTINUM:
No pathologically enlarged mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes.

HEART:
Heart size is within normal limits. No pericardial effusion.

UPPER ABDOMEN:
Small hypodense lesion in the right hepatic lobe,
incompletely characterized.

IMPRESSION:
1. Interval increase in size of an 8 mm right upper lobe
   pulmonary nodule.
2. No thoracic lymphadenopathy.
3. Indeterminate hepatic lesion. Please refer to the
   separately performed CT abdomen and pelvis.

exam_name: CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST
report_text:
EXAM:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Abdominal discomfort. Indeterminate hepatic lesion seen on
same-day chest CT.

COMPARISON:
CT abdomen and pelvis dated 08/21/2024.

FINDINGS:
LOWER CHEST:
Mild bibasilar atelectasis.

LIVER:
1.4 cm low-attenuation lesion in hepatic segment VII,
unchanged from 2024 and compatible with a benign cyst.

PANCREAS:
No focal pancreatic lesion or pancreatic ductal dilatation.

KIDNEYS:
No hydronephrosis or suspicious renal mass.

LYMPH NODES:
No abdominal or pelvic lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION:
1. Stable benign hepatic cyst corresponding to the lesion
   identified on the same-day chest CT.
2. No suspicious abdominal or pelvic mass.

EXAM:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH, PA AND LATERAL

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Cough. Pulmonary nodule.

COMPARISON:
Chest radiograph 01/12/2026 and CT chest performed earlier
today.

FINDINGS:
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is within normal limits.

No focal airspace consolidation, pleural effusion, or
pneumothorax.

The small right upper lobe pulmonary nodule demonstrated on
CT is not well visualized radiographically.

IMPRESSION:
1. No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
2. Known right upper lobe pulmonary nodule is better
   demonstrated on same-day CT.

EXAM:
BILATERAL DIAGNOSTIC DIGITAL MAMMOGRAPHY

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Recall from screening mammography for possible left breast
asymmetry.

COMPARISON:
Prior mammograms dated 03/11/2025 and 02/28/2024.

BREAST COMPOSITION:
The breasts are heterogeneously dense.

FINDINGS:
RIGHT BREAST:
No suspicious mass, architectural distortion, or suspicious
calcifications.

LEFT BREAST:
Persistent 1.2 cm irregular high-density mass in the upper
outer breast at posterior depth with associated fine
pleomorphic calcifications spanning 1.6 cm.

IMPRESSION:
Suspicious left breast mass with associated calcifications.
Targeted ultrasound and tissue sampling are recommended.

BI-RADS:
Category 4 - Suspicious abnormality.

EXAM:
CT CHEST WITHOUT IV CONTRAST

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Pulmonary nodule follow-up.

FINDINGS:
6 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the posterior right upper
lobe. No focal pulmonary consolidation.

No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:
6 mm right upper lobe pulmonary nodule.
Follow-up chest CT recommended.

EXAM:
CT PULMONARY ANGIOGRAM

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Acute shortness of breath and chest pain.

FINDINGS:
No filling defect within the pulmonary arteries to suggest
acute pulmonary embolism.

7 mm right upper lobe pulmonary nodule is noted.

Mild dependent bibasilar atelectasis.

No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:
1. No pulmonary embolism.
2. Right upper lobe pulmonary nodule. Follow-up according
   to clinical risk factors is recommended.

EXAM:
PORTABLE AP CHEST

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Shortness of breath.

FINDINGS:
Low lung volumes with mild bibasilar linear opacity,
favored to represent atelectatic change.

No focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:
Mild bibasilar atelectatic change. No acute focal
cardiopulmonary abnormality.

EXAM:
LEFT DIAGNOSTIC MAMMOGRAPHY

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Further evaluation of left breast mass and calcifications.

FINDINGS:
Irregular mass with associated pleomorphic calcifications
again identified in the upper outer left breast.

IMPRESSION:
Persistent suspicious left breast mass and calcifications.

BI-RADS:
Category 4 - Suspicious abnormality.

EXAM:
CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Follow-up hepatic lesion.

FINDINGS:
Stable 1.4 cm low-attenuation lesion in hepatic segment VII
compatible with a cyst.

No suspicious liver lesion.

Visualized lung bases demonstrate mild dependent
atelectatic change.

IMPRESSION:
Stable benign hepatic cyst.

EXAM:
CT CHEST WITHOUT IV CONTRAST

CLINICAL HISTORY:
Pulmonary nodule.

COMPARISON:
CT chest 05/14/2026.

FINDINGS:
8 mm right upper lobe pulmonary nodule is unchanged.

No new suspicious pulmonary nodule.

No focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:
Stable 8 mm right upper lobe pulmonary nodule.
